left: SELECT CASE WHEN qty = 2 THEN 'two' ELSE NULL END FROM items
right: SELECT CASE WHEN qty = 2 THEN 'two' END FROM items
label: equivalent
note: A CASE with no matching branch and no ELSE returns NULL.
claim: ELSE NULL in a CASE is redundant

left: SELECT CASE WHEN qty > 0 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END FROM items
right: SELECT COALESCE(qty > 0, FALSE) FROM items
label: equivalent
note: NULL qty gives FALSE on both sides.
claim: a CASE returning booleans can be a COALESCE of the condition

left: SELECT CASE WHEN qty IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE qty END FROM items
right: SELECT COALESCE(qty, 0) FROM items
label: equivalent
claim: a CASE testing IS NULL can be a COALESCE

left: SELECT CASE WHEN kind = 'a' THEN 1 ELSE CASE WHEN kind = 'b' THEN 2 END END FROM items
right: SELECT CASE WHEN kind = 'a' THEN 1 WHEN kind = 'b' THEN 2 END FROM items
label: equivalent
claim: a nested CASE in ELSE can be flattened

left: SELECT o.cid, o.total, c.region FROM orders AS o JOIN (SELECT cid, region FROM customers) AS c USING (cid)
right: WITH c AS (SELECT cid, region FROM customers) SELECT o.cid, o.total, c.region FROM orders AS o JOIN c USING (cid)
label: equivalent
claim: a subquery in a join can be a CTE

left: SELECT o.total, c.region FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c USING (cid)
right: SELECT o.total, c.region FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.cid = c.cid
label: equivalent
claim: USING can be spelled as ON

left: SELECT IFNULL(qty, 0) FROM items
right: SELECT COALESCE(qty, 0) FROM items
label: equivalent
claim: IFNULL is COALESCE

left: SELECT COUNT(1) FROM items
right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM items
label: equivalent
claim: COUNT(1) is COUNT(*)

left: SELECT id FROM items WHERE qty = NULL
right: SELECT id FROM items WHERE qty IS NULL
label: not_equivalent
note: = NULL is never true, so the left side returns no rows; IS NULL returns the NULL rows. The rule fixes a bug: the two are not equivalent.
claim: = NULL should be IS NULL

left: (SELECT id FROM items)
right: SELECT id FROM items
label: equivalent
claim: outer parentheses around a query are redundant

left: SELECT o.total, c.region FROM orders AS o RIGHT JOIN customers AS c ON o.cid = c.cid
right: SELECT o.total, c.region FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.cid = c.cid
label: equivalent
claim: RIGHT JOIN can be a LEFT JOIN with the tables swapped

left: SELECT o.total, c.region FROM orders AS o, customers AS c WHERE o.cid = c.cid
right: SELECT o.total, c.region FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.cid = c.cid
label: equivalent
claim: an implicit comma join can be an explicit JOIN

left: SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE closed = FALSE
right: SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE NOT closed
label: equivalent
note: NULL is dropped on both sides.
claim: compare booleans without = FALSE

left: SELECT id item_id FROM items
right: SELECT id AS item_id FROM items
label: equivalent
claim: write AS for aliases

left: SELECT orders.id, customers.region FROM orders LEFT JOIN customers USING (cid)
right: SELECT orders.id, customers.region FROM orders LEFT JOIN customers ON orders.cid = customers.cid
label: equivalent
claim: LEFT JOIN USING spelled with ON

left: SELECT id FROM notes WHERE REGEXP_CONTAINS(body, '.*abc.*')
right: SELECT id FROM notes WHERE body LIKE '%abc%'
label: equivalent
note: REGEXP_CONTAINS finds a match anywhere; .* may match nothing, so both test for the substring.
claim: LIKE instead of REGEXP_CONTAINS for a plain substring

left: SELECT id, grp, seq FROM (SELECT id, grp, seq, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY grp ORDER BY seq) AS rn FROM events) AS q WHERE rn = 1
right: SELECT id, grp, seq FROM events WHERE TRUE QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY grp ORDER BY seq) = 1
label: equivalent
note: (grp, seq) is a key, so ROW_NUMBER has no ties to break.
claim: QUALIFY replaces a filtered ROW_NUMBER subquery

left: SELECT h.code, h.price FROM prices AS h JOIN (SELECT code, MAX(since) AS m FROM prices GROUP BY code) AS x ON h.code = x.code AND h.since = x.m
right: SELECT code, price FROM prices WHERE TRUE QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY code ORDER BY since DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
note: A NULL code never joins on the left, but RANK keeps its latest row on the right.
claim: latest row per key: MAX join replaced by RANK

left: SELECT x, y FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT x, y FROM b
right: SELECT DISTINCT x, y FROM (SELECT x, y FROM a UNION ALL SELECT x, y FROM b)
label: equivalent
note: BigQuery requires DISTINCT or ALL; written as UNION DISTINCT and as DISTINCT over UNION ALL.
claim: UNION means UNION DISTINCT

left: SELECT region, shop, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY region, 2
right: SELECT region, shop, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY region, shop
label: equivalent
claim: do not mix positional and named GROUP BY

left: SELECT x, y FROM a, b
right: SELECT x, y FROM a CROSS JOIN b
label: equivalent
claim: a comma join without a condition is a CROSS JOIN

left: SELECT SUM(total) FROM orders WHERE CAST(ordered_at AS DATE) = DATE '2020-01-01'
right: SELECT SUM(total) FROM orders WHERE ordered_at BETWEEN TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01 00:00:00' AND TIMESTAMP '2020-12-31 23:59:59'
label: not_equivalent
note: An order on 2020-06-30 counts only on the right.
claim: replace a cast on a timestamp column by a range filter (the documented range spans a year, not the day)

left: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM sales WHERE region_key IN (SELECT region_key FROM regions WHERE state = 'CA')
right: SELECT SUM(s.amount) FROM sales AS s JOIN regions AS r ON r.region_key = s.region_key AND r.state = 'CA'
label: not_equivalent
note: Two CA rows with one region_key count each sale twice on the right.
claim: replace IN (subquery) by a join

left: SELECT p.name, SUM(s.amount) FROM sales AS s JOIN products AS p ON p.product_key = s.product_key WHERE s.sold_on > TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY p.name
right: SELECT p.name, SUM(s.amount) FROM sales AS s JOIN products AS p ON p.product_key = s.product_key AND p.added_on > TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01 00:00:00' WHERE s.sold_on > TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY p.name
label: not_equivalent
note: A product added before the date drops out on the right. The documented query also names an undefined alias; written here with the alias fixed and a GROUP BY.
claim: push a date filter to the joined table (the documented rewrite adds a condition on another column)

left: SELECT id, name, code FROM products WHERE SUBSTR(code, 1, 3) = 'HN-'
right: SELECT id, name, code FROM products WHERE name LIKE 'Hex%'
label: not_equivalent
note: A product coded HN-1 named Bolt is only on the left.
claim: make a filter sargable (the documented rewrite tests a different column)
